about.title: About DYNMECH CycleView
about.description: DYNMECH CycleView is a free tool for visualising equipment motion timing: design, check and present the action sequence of every mechanism on a machine and the cycle time they add up to.
about.license: Free software, no licence key required. Source code is released under the Apache License 2.0.

help.title: Keyboard Shortcuts
help.description: Use the following keyboard shortcuts to operate CycleView more efficiently

tips.title: Usage Tips
tips.tip1: Double-click the toolbar to toggle fullscreen mode
tips.tip2: Double-click a cell in the parameter table to edit it
tips.tip3: Hold Ctrl/Cmd and scroll to zoom the chart
tips.tip4: Turn on Follow Playback (F) so large charts keep the moving modules in view

help.inputNote: Shortcuts are paused while typing in a table cell

userGuide.title: User Guide
userGuide.introduction: CycleView is a professional mechanism motion timing visualization tool for simulating and analyzing the motion timing of mechanical equipment. This guide will help you get started quickly and make full use of CycleView features.

quickStart.title: Quick Start
quickStart.step1: Click the import icon (Ctrl+I) and choose a CSV file
quickStart.step2: Press Space to play; turn on Follow Playback (F) for large charts
quickStart.step3: Export a PDF report or a follow-playback MP4 (Ctrl+E)

gettingStarted.title: Getting Started
gettingStarted.step1: After launching CycleView, you'll see the main interface with a parameter table, canvas, and toolbar.
gettingStarted.step2: The parameter table on the left shows detailed information for all modules, including module names, action descriptions, and timing parameters.
gettingStarted.step3: The canvas area on the right displays the mechanism motion timing relationships in a visual format.
gettingStarted.step4: The toolbar holds import and export, playback with speed and follow, and view zoom; settings, help and language are on the right.

importingData.title: Importing Data
importingData.csvFormat: Import a CSV via the toolbar icon or Ctrl+I. Columns: module, action, startPosition, moveCount, duration; stage is optional.
importingData.requiredColumns: startPosition is the starting cell, moveCount the number of cells, duration the milliseconds per cell. The legacy header intervalTime is still accepted.
importingData.sequential: Within a module, an action whose startPosition is 0 starts right where the previous action ended, so a sequence of actions needs no manual offsets.

animationControls.title: Animation Controls
animationControls.playPause: Use the play/pause button or spacebar to control animation playback.
animationControls.stop: Stop (S or Esc) halts playback and rewinds to the start.
animationControls.reset: Reset (R or Home) returns to the first frame; ← and → step one frame at a time.
animationControls.speed: Speed runs from 0.1x to 4x via the toolbar selector or + and -; Loop (Ctrl+L) replays continuously.
animationControls.follow: Follow Playback (F) scrolls and zooms the canvas so every module in motion stays in view; the stage column mirrors each action's progress.
animationControls.view: Zoom with Ctrl++ and Ctrl+- or Ctrl+wheel, fit the chart to the window with Ctrl+0, return to actual size with Ctrl+1; table rows scale with the chart.

visualization.title: Visualization Features
visualization.modules: Each module is represented by colored bars, with length representing execution time.
visualization.stages: The stage column in the table fills in real time: one bar per action, complete when that action ends.
visualization.timing: Timing relationships are shown through horizontal position and length, clearly displaying action execution order and overlap relationships.
visualization.colors: Color coding helps quickly identify actions from different modules and stages.

exporting.title: Export Functions
exporting.formats: Export formats: CSV, PDF and MP4.
exporting.csv: CSV export writes the parameter table back out, optionally with the calculated start positions of sequential actions.
exporting.pdf: PDF export provides high-quality report format.
exporting.video: MP4 export records follow playback as a video: the camera scrolls and zooms so every active module stays in frame.

additionalHelp.title: Additional Help
additionalHelp.shortcuts: View keyboard shortcuts to improve operation efficiency.
additionalHelp.about: The About page contains application version and developer information.
additionalHelp.support: CycleView is a free tool and does not come with one-to-one technical support. Please consult this guide or visit dynmech.com.

gantt.title: Action Timing Gantt
gantt.sideHint: Click to select, double-click to edit; arrows show the dependency chain.
gantt.colorHint: Used by Gantt bars, resource lanes, the Excel colour column and PDF. Tick to apply to the whole subtree; otherwise only this node changes.
gantt.name: Name
gantt.timeHint: Accepts 1234, 1234ms, 1.234s, 01:23.456. Changing any predecessor cascades to every successor start.
gantt.summaryHint: Summary row: bounds roll up from all descendants and cannot be edited directly.
gantt.noPreds: No predecessors yet; start is set by this task itself.
gantt.summaryNoDeps: Summary rows cannot have predecessors; set them on actions or sub-actions.
gantt.path: Sub-actions can be nested to any depth
gantt.confirmDelete: Delete this task, all its sub-actions and related dependencies?
gantt.nestHint: A sub-action can be the parent of another sub-action, with no depth limit.
gantt.groupFlowTip: View by module / mechanism / action hierarchy
gantt.groupResourceTip: View claims and conflicts by mechanism / motor

timeScale.title: Time scale & precision
timeScale.scaleHint: Scale can be 1 ms; all computation uses integer milliseconds.
timeScale.precisionHint: Minimum 1 ms; every instant snaps to a multiple of this value.
timeScale.note: Changing scale/precision re-quantises and cascades every successor start; Gantt, beat grid, PDF, MP4 and Excel all read the new values.
timeScale.cellWidthHint: Pixels per scale division; larger stretches the time axis, same as toolbar zoom.

excel.title: Gantt ⇄ Excel conversion
excel.intro: Sheet 1 is the exact millisecond table; sheet 2 expands the chart into time columns; sheet 3 stores settings, hierarchy and dependencies for round-trip import.
excel.verified: Verified {{count}} rows; chart and table data are consistent, no conflicts.
excel.imported: Imported {{count}} rows and re-scheduled from dependencies; chart and table are in sync.
excel.matrixLabelEveryHint: Set to N to merge every N ticks in the Gantt matrix header into one cell showing that span (e.g. 0ms–400ms); 0 = no merge, sparse labels only. Data bars always stay per-tick to keep timing exact.

resource.title: Resources
resource.managerHint: Each resource is defined once and shared by actions across all flows. Reference them in an action’s resource allocations — no need to recreate the mechanism in every flow.
resource.empty: No resources. Click + to add a mechanism/motor, then set claims on actions.
resource.conflictHint: Red marks a resource conflict (hint only — timing is not auto-changed). Click a conflict to jump to its action.
resource.allocHint: Claim windows are relative to this action’s start. When the action is pushed by dependencies, its claims move with it. Overlapping windows on one resource are flagged red in the resource view (hint only).
resource.invalidNumber: Offset and duration must be numbers
resource.zeroDuration: Duration must be > 0 (and within the action)

cycle.title: Fixed cycle settings
cycle.hint: Only one action template is stored. Projected cycles are read-only; editing any instance writes back to the template.
cycle.overrun: actions cross the cycle boundary; cross-cycle resource conflicts are marked in the resource view
cycle.within: All actions finish inside one cycle
